bodyHtml:
Use this guide to decide whether open-kritt belongs on your shortlist: start with its stated purpose, then check setup, activity signals, maintenance clues, and adoption risks.

What is open-kritt?

Orchestrate AI agents to find real vulnerabilities in code.

Evidence: github.com

Who should consider it?

This guide is most relevant to frontend developers evaluating tools in the JavaScript ecosystem. The source associates the project with agent, agents, ai, bug bounty. Treat it as a starting point for a shortlist, then compare the official documentation with your own requirements.

Evidence: github.com

Why is it getting attention?

The repository appeared in this feed because its recorded GitHub activity made it notable at collection time. Stars and forks indicate attention, not technical quality, security, or suitability.

At collection time, the official source recorded 346 GitHub stars, 75 forks, 18 open issues, and a last recorded source push on 2026-07-22.

Evidence: api.github.com

How to evaluate it

Open the official repository before trying open-kritt. Review its README, recent releases, issue tracker, security policy, and license, then test it in a non-production project that matches your environment.

Treat stars, forks, and issue counts as repository signals rather than proof of quality, security, maintenance, or suitability. Review documentation, releases, issues, security policy, and license.

Evidence: github.com, kritt.ai, github.com, api.github.com

Bottom line

open-kritt has enough public source information to warrant a closer look, but the available activity signals are not a recommendation. The useful next step is to verify fit against the official documentation and test the project for your own constraints.
